[Classes > Sorcerer Subclass: Draconic Sorcery]
### Sorcerer Subclass: Draconic Sorcery  
_Breathe the Magic of Dragons_  
Your innate magic comes from the gift of a dragon. Perhaps an ancient dragon facing death bequeathed some of its magical power to you or your ancestor. You might have absorbed magic from a site infused with dragons' power. Or perhaps you handled a treasure taken from a dragon's hoard that was steeped in draconic power. Or you might have a dragon for an ancestor.

---

[Spells > Sorcerous Burst]
If you roll an 8 on a d8 for this spell, you can roll another d8, and add it to the damage. When you cast this spell, the maximum number of these d8s you can add to the spell's damage equals your spellcasting ability modifier.  
_Cantrip Upgrade._ The damage increases by 1d8 when you reach levels 5 (2d8), 11 (3d8), and 17 (4d8).

---

[Classes > Level 1: Arcane Recovery]
#### Level 1: Arcane Recovery  
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you're a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels' worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.

## o21 (Class) Which class has the highest hit points?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

**The Barbarian** has the highest hit points. It's the only class with a d12 hit die.

- **1st level:** 12 + Constitution modifier
- **Each level after:** 7 (the d12 average, rounded up) + Constitution modifier

For comparison, Fighter, Paladin, and Ranger use d10, and Bard, Cleric, Druid, Monk, Rogue, and Warlock use d8. Sorcerer and Wizard use d6, which gives them the fewest.

Thanks to your athleticism, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Strength (Athletics) checks.  
In addition, immediately after you score a Critical Hit, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

[Playing the Game > Hit Points]
### Hit Points  
Hit Points represent durability and the will to live. Creatures with more Hit Points are more difficult to kill. Your Hit Point maximum is the number of Hit Points you have when uninjured. Your current Hit Points can be any number from that maximum down to 0, which is the lowest Hit Points can go.  
Whenever you take damage, subtract it from your Hit Points. Hit Point loss has no effect on your capabilities until you reach 0 Hit Points.

[Playing the Game > Hit Points]
### Hit Points  
Hit Points represent durability and the will to live. Creatures with more Hit Points are more difficult to kill. Your Hit Point maximum is the number of Hit Points you have when uninjured. Your current Hit Points can be any number from that maximum down to 0, which is the lowest Hit Points can go.  
Whenever you take damage, subtract it from your Hit Points. Hit Point loss has no effect on your capabilities until you reach 0 Hit Points.

---

[Rules Glossary > Hit Points]
#### Hit Points  
Hit Points (HP) are a measure of how difficult it is to kill or destroy a creature or an object. Damage reduces Hit Points, and healing restores them. You can't have more Hit Points than your Hit Point maximum, and you can't have less than 0. _See also_ "Breaking Objects" and "Playing the Game" ("Damage and Healing").

---

[Classes > Level 3: Remarkable Athlete]
#### Level 3: Remarkable Athlete  
Thanks to your athleticism, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Strength (Athletics) checks.  
In addition, immediately after you score a Critical Hit, you can move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

## o22 (Class) How does a Rogue perform Sneak Attack?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

**Sneak Attack** is a Rogue feature that adds extra damage to one attack per turn.

**Requirements (all of these must be met):**
1. **Weapon type:** The attack is a weapon attack with a **Finesse** or **Ranged** weapon.
2. **Positioning:** You have **advantage** on the attack roll, **or** an ally of yours is within 5 feet of the target and isn't incapacitated. (You can't use this if you have disadvantage on the roll.)
3. **Frequency:** You can use Sneak Attack **once per turn**.

**Damage:** The extra damage is a number of d6s based on your Rogue level, starting at **1d6** at level 1 and increasing by 1d6 at every odd Rogue level (2d6 at 3rd, 3d6 at 5th, and so on). The extra damage is the same type as the weapon's damage. On a critical hit, roll the Sneak Attack dice twice.


### v1_baseline  (3 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

A Rogue performs Sneak Attack by hitting a creature with an attack roll, once per turn, while:

- **Having Advantage** on the roll.
- **Using a Finesse or Ranged weapon** for the attack.

If these conditions are met, the Rogue deals an extra 1d6 damage to that creature. The extra damage has the same type as the weapon.

The Context doesn't say how the Rogue gets Advantage, so that part is missing. It also doesn't state how Sneak Attack damage scales beyond 1d6 at higher levels. Cunning Strike (Level 5) lets the Rogue spend Sneak Attack dice to add effects, but the Context doesn't say how many dice the Rogue has.

[Classes > Level 1: Sneak Attack]
#### Level 1: Sneak Attack  
You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type.

---

[Classes > Level 5: Cunning Strike]
#### Level 5: Cunning Strike  
You've developed cunning ways to use your Sneak Attack. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects. Each effect has a die cost, which is the number of Sneak Attack damage dice you must forgo to add the effect. You remove the die before rolling, and the effect occurs immediately after the attack's damage is dealt. For example, if you add the Poison effect, remove 1d6 from the Sneak Attack's damage before rolling.

You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type.

When you score a Critical Hit, you deal extra damage. Roll the attack's damage dice twice, add them together, and add any relevant modifiers as normal. For example, if you score a Critical Hit with a Dagger, roll 2d4 for the damage rather than 1d4, and add your relevant ability modifier. If the attack involves other damage dice, such as from the Rogue's Sneak Attack feature, you also roll those dice twice.

## o23 (Class) What are the special abilities of a Druid?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

Here are a Druid's core special abilities in the 2024 rules. I'm working from memory, so check the exact wording and level thresholds against the SRD 5.2 if precision matters.

- **Druidic (Level 1):** Druids know Druidic, a secret language. They can also leave hidden messages in ordinary conversation that only other Druids notice.
- **Primal Order (Level 1):** You choose a path that fits your druid's role. *Magician* grants extra spell-related benefits, and *Warden* grants combat-oriented proficiencies.
- **Spellcasting (Level 1):** Druids cast prepared spells from the druid spell list using Wisdom as their spellcasting ability.
- **Wild Shape (Level 2):** You can magically transform into a beast you've seen. Your beast forms are limited by challenge rating and movement options, which expand as you level up. You regain uses on a long rest.
- **Wild Companion (Level 2):** You can spend a Wild Shape use to summon a spirit familiar that takes a beast-like form, helping with tasks and scouting.
- **Druid Circle (Level 3):** You choose a circle subclass, which grants additional features at Level 3 and beyond.
- **Ability Score Improvements:** Standard increases at the usual levels.
- **Timeless Body (Level 18):** Your aging slows, and you need less food and drink.
- **Beast Spells (Level 18):** You can cast spells while in a Wild Shape form, though you can't cast with verbal or material components unless your form allows it.
- **Archdruid (Level 20):** You regain Wild Shape uses on a short rest, and you can use Wild Shape without expending a use a limited number of times.

### v6_agentic  (16 chunks, 3 LLM call(s))

Based on the Context, a Druid has these special abilities:

- **Spellcasting (Level 1):** Druids can learn cantrips and replace one whenever they gain a Druid level. They gain another cantrip at Druid levels 4 and 10. They cast level 1+ spells using spell slots, which regain on a Long Rest. The number of prepared spells increases with level.
- **Wild Shape (Level 2):** As a Bonus Action, you can shape-shift into a Beast form you have learned. You stay in that form for half your Druid level in hours, or until you use Wild Shape again, become Incapacitated, or die. You can also leave the form early as a Bonus Action. You can use Wild Shape twice, regaining one use on a Short Rest and all uses on a Long Rest. When you assume a form, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Druid level.
- **Druid Subclass (Level 3):** You choose a subclass. The Context describes only the Circle of the Land. Each Long Rest, you choose a land type (arid, polar, temperate, or tropical) and have the spells for your level prepared from that land's list. Examples:
  - Arid: Blur, Burning Hands, and Fire Bolt at level 3; Fireball at level 5.
  - Temperate: Misty Step, Shocking Grasp, and Sleep at level 3; Lightning Bolt at level 5; Freedom of Movement at level 7; Tree Stride at level 9.

**Missing from the Context:**
- The full Druid Features table is cut off, so the number of Wild Shape uses at higher levels, the spell slots per level, and the prepared-spell counts beyond the rows shown are unavailable.
- The Tropical spell list is cut off, and the Polar list is not included.
- The Known Forms rules for Wild Shape are referenced but not provided.
- The Circle of the Land's other subclass features are not included.
- Other Level 1 features, and the Archdruid feature at level 20, are not described.

[Classes > Level 3: Druid Subclass]
#### Level 3: Druid Subclass  
You gain a Druid subclass of your choice. The Circle of the Land subclass is detailed after this class's description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Druid levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Druid level or lower.

---

[Character Creation > Prerequisites]
### Prerequisites  
To qualify for a new class, you must have a score of at least 13 in the primary ability of the new class and your current classes. For example, a Barbarian who decides to multiclass into the Druid class must have Strength and Wisdom scores of 13 or higher, since Strength is the primary ability for Barbarians and Wisdom is the primary ability for Druids.

---

[Classes > As a Multiclass Character]

• Gain the following traits from the Core Druid Traits table: Hit Point Die and training with Light armor and Shields.
• Gain the Druid's level 1 features, which are listed in the Druid Features table. See the multiclassing rules in "Character Creation" to determine your available spell slots.

[Classes > Level 2: Wild Shape]
#### Level 2: Wild Shape  
The power of nature allows you to assume the form of an animal. As a Bonus Action, you shape-shift into a Beast form that you have learned for this feature (see "Known Forms" below). You stay in that form for a number of hours equal to half your Druid level or until you use Wild Shape again, have the Incapacitated condition, or die. You can also leave the form early as a Bonus Action.

---

[Classes > Level 2: Wild Shape]
_Number of Uses._ You can use Wild Shape twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.  
You gain additional uses when you reach certain Druid levels, as shown in the Wild Shape column of the Druid Features table.

---

[Classes > Level 2: Wild Shape]
**Temporary Hit Points.** When you assume a Wild Shape form, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Druid level.

### Druid Subclass: Circle of the Land  
_Celebrate Connection to the Natural World_  
The Circle of the Land comprises mystics and sages who safeguard ancient knowledge and rites. These Druids meet within sacred circles of trees or standing stones to whisper primal secrets in Druidic. The circle's wisest members preside as the chief priests of their communities.

[Magic Items > Mysterious Deck]
_Void._ Your soul is drawn from your body and contained in an object in a place of the GM's choice. One or more powerful beings guard the place. While your soul is trapped in this way, your body is inert, ceases aging, and requires no food, air, or water. A _Wish_ spell can't return your soul to your body, but the spell reveals the location of the object that holds your soul. You draw no more cards.

---

[Spells > Magic Jar]
Your body falls into a catatonic state as your soul leaves it and enters the container you used for the spell's Material component. While your soul inhabits the container, you are aware of your surroundings as if you were in the container's space. You can't move or take Reactions. The only action you can take is to project your soul up to 100 feet out of the container, either returning to your living body (and ending the spell) or attempting to possess a Humanoid's body.

---

[Spells > Magic Jar]
While possessing a body, you can take a Magic action to return from the host body to the container if it is within 100 feet of you, returning the host creature's soul to its body. If the host body dies while you're in it, the creature dies, and you make a Charisma saving throw against your own spellcasting DC. On a success, you return to the container if it is within 100 feet of you. Otherwise, you die.

---

[Classes > Level 1: Spellcasting]
Whenever you gain a Druid level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Druid spell list.  
When you reach Druid levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Druid spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Druid Features table.  
_Spell Slots._ The Druid Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

---

[Classes > Level 1: Spellcasting]
The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Druid levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Druid Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Druid spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Druid, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

## o24 (Class) Can a Fighter cast spells?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

**Not by default, but yes in a few ways:**

- **Eldritch Knight (Fighter subclass):** Gains spellcasting at 3rd level, using Intelligence as its spellcasting ability. It's a third-caster progression, and its spells come from the Wizard spell list. Check the subclass text for any school restrictions on which spells it can learn.
- **Magic Initiate (feat):** Gives a few cantrips and a level 1 spell from a chosen class list. A Fighter can take it, usually as an Origin feat.
- **Multiclassing:** A Fighter can take levels in a spellcasting class to gain spell slots and spells.
- **Magic items:** Spell scrolls and other magic items can let a Fighter cast spells, subject to the item's rules.


### v1_baseline  (3 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

The only "No Spellcasting" text is under "Classes > Level 2: Wild Shape," but that excerpt doesn't name the class it belongs to, so I can't attribute it to Fighters. The other entries (Spell Attack and Casting without Slots) don't address class eligibility.

#### Spellcasting  
If a monster can cast any spells, its stat block lists the spells and provides the monster's spellcasting ability, spell save DC (if any spells require a saving throw), and spell attack bonus (if any spells require an attack roll). [Spells > Casting Spells]
## Casting Spells  
Each spell description has a series of entries that provide the details needed to cast the spell. The following sections explain each of those entries, which follow a spell's name.  
> **Casting in Armor**
>
> You must have training with any armor you are wearing to cast spells while wearing it. You are otherwise too hampered by the armor for spellcasting.

---

[Spells > Animal Shapes]
A target's game statistics are replaced by the chosen Beast's statistics, but the target retains its creature type; Hit Points; Hit Point Dice; alignment; ability to communicate; and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores. The target's actions are limited by the Beast form's anatomy, and it can't cast spells. The target's equipment melds into the new form, and the target can't use any of that equipment while in that form.

---

[Spells > Casting without Slots]
**Special Abilities.** Some characters and monsters have special abilities that allow them to cast specific spells without a spell slot. This casting is usually limited in another way, such as being able to cast the spell a limited number of times per day.  
**Magic Items.** _Spell Scrolls_ and some other magic items contain spells that can be cast without a spell slot. The description of such an item specifies how many times a spell can be cast from it.

---

[Classes > Level 18: Beast Spells]
#### Level 18: Beast Spells  
While using Wild Shape, you can cast spells in Beast form, except for any spell that has a Material component with a cost specified or that consumes its Material component.

---

[Spells > Casting without Slots]
**Rituals.** Certain spells have the Ritual tag in the Casting Time entry. Such a spell can be cast following the normal rules for spellcasting, or it can be cast as a Ritual. The Ritual version of a spell takes 10 minutes longer to cast than normal, but it doesn't expend a spell slot. To cast a spell as a Ritual, a spellcaster must have it prepared.

---

[Character Creation > Spellcasting]
This table might give you spell slots of a higher level than the spells you prepare. You can use those slots but only to cast your lower-level spells. If a lower-level spell that you cast, like _Burning Hands_, has an enhanced effect when cast at a higher level, you can use the enhanced effect as normal.

### Fighter Subclass: Champion  
_Pursue Physical Excellence in Combat_  
A Champion focuses on the development of martial prowess in a relentless pursuit of victory. Champions combine rigorous training with physical excellence to deal devastating blows, withstand peril, and garner glory. Whether in athletic contests or bloody battle, Champions strive for the crown of the victor.

[Classes > Level 20: Eldritch Master]
#### Level 20: Eldritch Master  
When you use your Magical Cunning feature, you regain all your expended Pact Magic spell slots.

---

[Classes > Eldritch Spear]
#### Eldritch Spear  
_Prerequisite: Level 2+ Warlock, a Warlock Cantrip That Deals Damage_  
Choose one of your known Warlock cantrips that deals damage and has a range of 10+ feet. When you cast that spell, its range increases by a number of feet equal to 30 times your Warlock level.  
_Repeatable._ You can gain this invocation more than once. Each time you do so, choose a different eligible cantrip.

---

[Classes > Eldritch Smite]
#### Eldritch Smite  
_Prerequisite: Level 5+ Warlock, Pact of the Blade Invocation_  
Once per turn when you hit a creature with your pact weapon, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to deal an extra 1d8 Force damage to the target,
plus another 1d8 per level of the spell slot, and you can give the target the Prone condition if it is Huge or smaller.

---

[Spells > Arcane Sword]
On your later turns, you can take a Bonus Action to move the sword up to 30 feet to a spot you can see and repeat the attack against the same target or a different one.

---

[Spells > Arcane Hand]
**Forceful Hand.** The hand attempts to push a Huge or smaller creature within 5 feet of it. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw, or the hand pushes the target up to 5 feet plus a number of feet equal to five times your spellcasting ability modifier. The hand moves with the target, remaining within 5 feet of it.

---

[Spells > Arcane Hand]
**Grasping Hand.** The hand attempts to grapple a Huge or smaller creature within 5 feet of it. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, or the target has the Grappled condition, with an escape DC equal to your spell save DC. While the hand grapples the target, you can take a Bonus Action to cause the hand to crush it, dealing Bludgeoning damage to the target equal to 4d6 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

---

[Character Creation > Spellcasting]
Then look up this total level in the Level column of the Multiclass Spellcaster table. You use the slots for that level to cast spells of an appropriate level from any class whose Spellcasting feature you have.

---

[Character Creation > Spellcasting]
#### Spellcasting  
Your capacity for spellcasting depends partly on your combined levels in all your spellcasting classes and partly on your individual levels in those classes. Once you have the Spellcasting feature from more than one class, use the rules below. If you multiclass but have the Spellcasting feature from only one class, follow the rules for that class.

---

[Character Creation > Spellcasting]
_Pact Magic._ If you have the Pact Magic feature from the Warlock class and the Spellcasting feature, you can use the spell slots you gain from Pact Magic to cast spells you have prepared from classes with the Spellcasting feature, and you can use the spell slots you gain from the Spellcasting feature to cast Warlock spells you have prepared.

#### Spellcasting Focus  
A Spellcasting Focus is an object that certain creatures can use in place of a spell's Material components if those materials aren't consumed by the spell and don't have a cost specified. Some classes allow its members to use certain types of Spellcasting Focuses. _See also_ "Spells" ("Casting Spells").

## o25 (Class) What are the subclasses available for Clerics?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

In the 2024 rules, Clerics choose a **Divine Domain** at 3rd level. The options are:

1. **Knowledge**
2. **Life**
3. **Light**
4. **Nature**
5. **Tempest**
6. **Trickery**
7. **War**

Clerics also pick a **Divine Order** at 1st level (Protector or Thaumaturge), but that is a separate choice, not a subclass. I'm not fully certain which of these the SRD 5.2 includes, so check the document if you need to confirm.

_Soothe the Hurts of the World_  
The Life Domain focuses on the positive energy that helps sustain all life in the multiverse. Clerics who tap into this domain are masters of healing, using that life force to cure many hurts.

---

[Classes > Cleric Subclass: Life Domain]
Existence itself relies on the positive energy associated with this domain, so a Cleric of almost any religious tradition might choose it. This domain is particularly associated with agricultural deities, gods of healing or endurance, and gods of home and community. Religious orders of healing also seek the magic of this domain.

## o26 (Class) How does a Warlock regain spell slots?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

Warlocks use **Pact Magic**, which works differently from other casters:

- **Short Rest:** You regain *all* expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a short rest.
- **Long Rest:** You also regain all expended slots when you finish a long rest.

Warlocks have few slots, but each is cast at the highest level they've reached, so a short rest is usually enough to recover fully. Mystic Arcanum spells, if you have them, are a separate pool that refreshes only on a long rest.


### v1_baseline  (3 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

A Warlock regains all expended Pact Magic spell slots when they finish a Short or Long Rest.

*retrieved sections:* Classes > Level 1: Pact Magic | Spells > Spell Slots | Character Creation > Spellcasting

[Classes > Level 1: Pact Magic]
_Spell Slots._ The Warlock Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1–5. The table also shows the level of those slots, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a Short or Long Rest.  
For example, when you're a level 5 Warlock, you have two level 3 spell slots. To cast the level 1 spell _Charm Person_, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a level 3 spell.

---

[Spells > Spell Slots]
Finishing a Long Rest restores any expended spell slots.

_Pact Magic._ If you have the Pact Magic feature from the Warlock class and the Spellcasting feature, you can use the spell slots you gain from Pact Magic to cast spells you have prepared from classes with the Spellcasting feature, and you can use the spell slots you gain from the Spellcasting feature to cast Warlock spells you have prepared.

### v4_hybrid  (8 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

A Warlock regains expended Pact Magic spell slots in two ways:

1. **Resting:** When you finish a Short Rest or a Long Rest, you regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots.
2. **Magical Cunning (Level 2):** You can perform an esoteric rite that takes 1 minute. At the end, you regain expended Pact Magic spell slots, up to a number equal to half your maximum (round up). You can use this feature only once, and you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

The Context doesn't say how slots from the Spellcasting feature are regained if you have multiclassed into another spellcasting class, because that part of the text is cut off.

[Classes > Level 1: Pact Magic]
#### Level 1: Pact Magic  
Through occult ceremony, you have formed a pact with a mysterious entity to gain magical powers. The entity is a voice in the shadows—its identity unclear—but its boon to you is concrete: the ability to cast spells. See "Spells" for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Warlock spells, which appear in the Warlock spell list later in the class's description.

---

[Classes > Level 1: Pact Magic]
_Spell Slots._ The Warlock Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your Warlock spells of levels 1–5. The table also shows the level of those slots, all of which are the same level. You regain all expended Pact Magic spell slots when you finish a Short or Long Rest.  
For example, when you're a level 5 Warlock, you have two level 3 spell slots. To cast the level 1 spell _Charm Person_, you must spend one of those slots, and you cast it as a level 3 spell.

---

[Classes > Level 1: Pact Magic]
The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Warlock levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Warlock Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Warlock spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level no higher than what's shown in the table's Slot Level column for your level. When you reach level 6, for example, you learn a new Warlock spell, which can be of levels 1–3.

---

[Classes > Level 1: Arcane Recovery]
#### Level 1: Arcane Recovery  
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you're a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels' worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.

---

[Classes > Level 6: Natural Recovery]
In addition, when you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your Druid level (round up), and none of them can be level 6+. For example, if you're a level 6 Druid, you can recover up to three levels' worth of spell slots. You can recover a level 3 spell slot, a level 2 and a level 1 spell slot, or three level 1 spell slots. Once you recover spell slots with this feature, you can't do so

---

[Classes > Level 20: Eldritch Master]
#### Level 20: Eldritch Master  
When you use your Magical Cunning feature, you regain all your expended Pact Magic spell slots.

---

[Classes > Level 1: Pact Magic]
_Prepared Spells of Level 1+._ You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Warlock spells. _Charm Person_ and _Hex_ are recommended.

---

[Rules Glossary > Short Rest]
#### Short Rest  
A Short Rest is a 1-hour period of downtime, during which a creature does nothing more strenuous than reading, talking, eating, or standing watch. To start a Short Rest, you must have at least 1 Hit Point.  
_Benefits of the Rest._ When you finish the rest, you gain the following benefits:

---

[Rules Glossary > Short Rest]
_Interrupting the Rest._ A Short Rest is stopped by the following interruptions:  
- Rolling Initiative
- Casting a spell other than a cantrip
- Taking any damage  
An interrupted Short Rest confers no benefits.

---

[Rules Glossary > Short Rest]
**Spend Hit Point Dice.** You can spend one or more of your Hit Point Dice to regain Hit Points. For each Hit Point Die you spend in this way, roll the die and add your Constitution modifier to it. You regain Hit Points equal to the total (minimum of 1 Hit Point). You can decide to spend an additional Hit Point Die after each roll.  
**Special Feature.** Some features are recharged by a Short Rest. If you have such a feature, it recharges in the way specified in its description.

---

[Rules Glossary > Long Rest]
#### Long Rest  
A Long Rest is a period of extended downtime—at least 8 hours—available to any creature. During a Long Rest, you sleep for at least 6 hours and perform no more than 2 hours of light activity, such as reading, talking, eating, or standing watch.  
During sleep, you have the Unconscious condition. After you finish a Long Rest, you must wait at least 16 hours before starting another one.

---

[Rules Glossary > Long Rest]
You can resume a Long Rest immediately after an interruption. If you do so, the rest requires 1 additional hour per interruption to finish.

---

[Rules Glossary > Long Rest]
_Benefits of the Rest._ To start a Long Rest, you must have at least 1 Hit Point. When you finish the rest, you gain the following benefits:  
**Regain All HP.** You regain all lost Hit Points and all spent Hit Point Dice. If your Hit Point maximum was reduced, it returns to normal.  
**Ability Scores Restored.** If any of your ability scores were reduced, they return to normal.  
**Exhaustion Reduced.** If you have the Exhaustion condition, its level decreases by 1.

---

[Classes > Level 11: Mystic Arcanum]
As shown in the Warlock Features table, you gain another Warlock spell of your choice that can be cast in this way when you reach Warlock levels 13 (level 7 spell), 15 (level 8 spell), and 17 (level 9 spell). You regain all uses of your Mystic Arcanum when you finish a Long Rest.  
Whenever you gain a Warlock level, you can replace one of your arcanum spells with another Warlock spell of the same level.

---

[Classes > Level 11: Mystic Arcanum]
#### Level 11: Mystic Arcanum  
Your patron grants you a magical secret called an arcanum. Choose one level 6 Warlock spell as this arcanum.  
You can cast your arcanum spell once without expending a spell slot, and you must finish a Long Rest before you can cast it in this way again.

### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

# Beholder (D&D 5e, CR 13 Aberration)

**Core traits**
- **Flight:** Hovers and flies slowly (fly speed about 20 ft.). It has no walking speed.
- **Antimagic Cone:** The large central eye creates an antimagic cone, a long cone in the direction it faces. Magic doesn't work inside it, and magical effects can't pass through it.
- **Darkvision:** Sees in the dark with a long range, around 120 ft.
- **Legendary Resistance:** Can choose to succeed on a failed saving throw a limited number of times per day.

**Actions**
- **Bite:** A melee attack that deals damage.
- **Eye Rays:** Each turn, it can fire a few of its smaller eye rays at targets within range. Each ray has a different effect, such as:
  - **Charm:** Charms a creature.
  - **Paralyzing:** Paralyzes a creature.
  - **Fear:** Frightens a creature.
  - **Slowing:** Slows a creature.
  - **Enervation:** Deals necrotic damage.
  - **Telekinetic:** Pushes or moves a creature.
  - **Sleep:** Puts a creature to sleep.
  - **Petrification:** Turns a creature to stone.
  - **Disintegration:** Destroys a creature or object.
  - **Death:** Kills a creature outright.

**Legendary Actions**
- It can take extra turn options (such as movement or additional eye rays) at the end of other creatures' turns.

I'm not certain of the exact numbers (damage dice, save DCs, uses per day, and legendary action counts) for the 2024 SRD 5.2 version. Check the stat block in the SRD for precise values.

### Ability Checks  
An ability check represents a creature using talent and training to try to overcome a challenge, such as forcing open a stuck door, picking a lock, entertaining a crowd, or deciphering a cipher. The GM and the rules often call for an ability check when a creature attempts something other than an attack that has a chance of meaningful failure. When the outcome is uncertain and narratively interesting, the dice determine the result.

[Playing the Game > Rhythm of Play]
This pattern holds during every game session (each time you sit down to play D&D), whether the adventurers are talking to a noble, exploring a ruin, or fighting a dragon. In certain situations—particularly combat—the action is more structured, and everyone takes turns.

---

[Playing the Game > Rhythm of Play]
# Playing the Game  
## Rhythm of Play  
The three main pillars of D&D play are social interaction, exploration, and combat. Whichever one you're experiencing, the game unfolds according to this basic pattern:  
**1: The Game Master Describes a Scene.** The GM tells the players where their adventurers are and what's around them (how many doors lead out of a room, what's on a table, and so on).

---

[Monsters A–Z > Actions]
&emsp;**At Will:** _Detect Magic, Mind Spike_ (level 5 version), _Minor Illusion, Shapechange_ (Beast or Humanoid form only, no Temporary Hit Points gained from the spell, and no Concentration or Temporary Hit Points required to maintain the spell) <br>
&emsp;**1/Day Each:** _Greater Restoration, Major Image, Project Image_

[Magic Items > Ring of X-ray Vision]
#### Ring of X-ray Vision  
_Ring, Rare (Requires Attunement)_  
While wearing this ring, you can take a Magic action to gain X-ray vision with a range of 30 feet for 1 minute. To you, solid objects within that radius appear transparent and don't prevent light from passing through them. The vision can penetrate 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or up to 3 feet of wood or dirt. Thicker substances or a thin sheet of lead block the vision.

_Level 7 Evocation (Bard, Sorcerer, Wizard)_  
**Casting Time:** Action
**Range:** Self
**Components:** V, S
**Duration:** Instantaneous  
Eight rays of light flash from you in a 60-foot Cone. Each creature in the Cone makes a Dexterity saving throw. For each target, roll 1d8 to determine which color ray affects it, consulting the Prismatic Rays table.

[Spells > Scorching Ray]
#### Scorching Ray  
_Level 2 Evocation (Sorcerer, Wizard)_  
**Casting Time:** Action
**Range:** 120 feet
**Components:** V, S
**Duration:** Instantaneous  
You hurl three fiery rays. You can hurl them at one target within range or at several. Make a ranged spell attack for each ray. On a hit, the target takes 2d6 Fire damage.  
_Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot._ You create one additional ray for each spell slot level above 2.

---

[Spells > Antimagic Field]
#### Antimagic Field  
_Level 8 Abjuration (Cleric, Wizard)_  
**Casting Time:** Action
**Range:** Self
**Components:** V, S, M (iron filings)
**Duration:** Concentration, up to 1 hour  
An aura of antimagic surrounds you in 10-foot Emanation. No one can cast spells, take Magic actions, or create other magical effects inside the aura, and those things can't target or otherwise affect anything inside it. Magical properties of magic items don't work inside the aura or on anything inside it.

---

[Spells > Antimagic Field]
Areas of effect created by spells or other magic can't extend into the aura, and no one can teleport into or out of it or use planar travel there. Portals close temporarily while in the aura.  
Ongoing spells, except those cast by an Artifact or a deity, are suppressed in the area. While an effect is suppressed, it doesn't function, but the time it spends suppressed counts against its duration.

---

[Spells > Antimagic Field]
_Dispel Magic_ has no effect on the aura, and the auras created by different _Antimagic Field_ spells don't nullify each other.

[Monsters > Legendary Actions]
### Legendary Actions  
If the monster has Legendary Action options, those are listed in this section. A Legendary Action is an action that a monster can take immediately after another creature's turn. Only one of these actions can be taken at a time and only after another creature's turn ends. The monster can't take a Legendary Action if it has the Incapacitated condition or is otherwise unable to take actions.

---

[Monsters A–Z > Legendary Actions]
#### Legendary Actions  
<hr>  
_Legendary Action Uses: 3 (4 in Lair). Immediately after another creature's turn, the aboleth can expend a use to take one of the following actions. The aboleth regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns._  
**_Lash._** The aboleth makes one Tentacle attack.  
**_Psychic Drain._** If the aboleth has at least one creature Charmed or Grappled, it uses Consume Memories and regains 5 (1d10) Hit Points.

[Rules Glossary > Telepathy]
#### Telepathy  
Telepathy is a magical ability that allows a creature to communicate mentally with another creature within a specified range. Unless a rule states otherwise, the contacted creature doesn't need to share a language with the telepath to understand this communication, but the contacted creature must be able to understand at least one language or be telepathic itself to understand.

[Rules Glossary > Armor Class]
#### Armor Class  
An Armor Class (AC) is the target number for an attack roll. AC represents how difficult it is to hit a target.  
Your base AC calculation is 10 plus your Dexterity modifier. If a rule gives you another base AC calculation, you choose which calculation to use; you can't use more than one. _See also_ "Attack Roll."

---

[Character Creation > Armor Class]
#### Armor Class  
If you have multiple ways to calculate your Armor Class, you can benefit from only one at a time. For example, a Monk/Sorcerer with a Monk's Unarmored Defense feature and a Sorcerer's Draconic Resilience feature must choose only one of those features as a way to calculate Armor Class.

## o29 (Monster) What damage types is a Troll vulnerable to?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

A Troll has **no damage vulnerabilities** in the 2024 SRD 5.2 rules. Its defense comes from **Regeneration** instead. Acid and fire damage stop that regeneration from working at the start of its next turn.


### v1_baseline  (3 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

The provided Context doesn't say what damage types a Troll is vulnerable to. It only covers Loathsome Limbs, Regeneration (which mentions Acid and Fire damage stopping the regeneration on the next turn, but not as vulnerabilities), and the general Damage and Healing heading, which contains no specifics. So the vulnerability information is missing from the Context.

[Monsters A–Z > Traits]
#### Traits  
<hr>  
**_Loathsome Limbs (4/Day)._** If the troll ends any turn Bloodied and took 15+ Slashing damage during that turn, one of the troll's limbs is severed, falls into the troll's space, and becomes a **Troll Limb**. The limb acts immediately after the troll's turn. The troll has 1 Exhaustion level for each missing limb, and it grows replacement limbs the next time it regains Hit Points.

---

[Monsters A–Z > Traits]
**_Regeneration._** The troll regains 15 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. If the troll takes Acid or Fire damage, this trait doesn't function on the troll's next turn. The troll dies only if it starts its turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

### Resistance and Vulnerability  
Some creatures and objects have Resistance or Vulnerability to certain damage types. If you have Resistance to a damage type, damage of that type is halved against you (round down). If you have Vulnerability to a damage type, damage of that type is doubled against you. For example, if you have Resistance to Cold damage, such damage is halved against you, and if you have Vulnerability to Fire damage, such damage is doubled against you.

---

[Rules Glossary > Vulnerability]
#### Vulnerability  
If you have Vulnerability to a damage type, damage of that type is doubled against you. Vulnerability is applied only once to an instance of damage. _See also_ "Playing the Game" ("Damage and Healing").

## o30 (Monster) How can a Vampire be defeated?

**Answerable from the SRD:** partial


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

A vampire can be defeated in several ways. The exact wording varies between the 2014 Monster Manual and the 2024 rules, so check your edition.

- **Overcome its damage resistances:** Vampires resist nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, so use magical or silvered weapons.
- **Stop its Regeneration:** A vampire regains hit points at the start of its turn unless it is in sunlight or running water. Radiant damage prevents Regeneration until its next turn, so radiant damage is especially effective.
- **Sunlight Hypersensitivity:** Sunlight deals radiant damage to it at the start of each of its turns while it is exposed.
- **Running water:** Being fully immersed in running water deals heavy damage to it.
- **Stake to the heart:** If a wooden piercing weapon is driven into its heart while it is incapacitated in its resting place (usually its coffin), it is paralyzed until the stake is removed. Destroying it in its coffin is a classic way to finish it off.
- **Forbiddance:** It cannot enter a residence without an invitation, which can limit its movement and options.

Note that vampires can also turn into mist or bats to escape, so pin them down or lock down their resting place before attacking.


### v1_baseline  (3 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

According to the Context, a vampire is destroyed by driving a weapon that deals Piercing damage into its heart while it has the Incapacitated condition. The Context doesn't say how to inflict the Incapacitated condition, and it doesn't say whether reducing the vampire to 0 hit points defeats it.

The Context also has a second, different version of Stake to the Heart. If the weapon is driven into the heart while the vampire is Incapacitated in its resting place, the vampire becomes Paralyzed until the weapon is removed. That version doesn't say the vampire is destroyed.

Sunlight and running water damage the vampire but don't defeat it, according to the Context.

According to the Context, a vampire can be defeated in these ways:

- **Stake to the Heart:** It is destroyed if a weapon that deals Piercing damage is driven into its heart while it has the Incapacitated condition.
- **Mist form at 0 HP:** If it is reduced to 0 Hit Points in mist form, it must reach its resting place within 2 hours or be destroyed.

The Context also lists weaknesses that deal damage but don't clearly destroy it:

- **Sunlight:** It takes 20 Radiant damage if it starts its turn in sunlight.
- **Running Water:** It takes 20 Acid damage if it ends its turn in running water.

The Context doesn't say what happens when a vampire in bat or vampire form reaches 0 Hit Points, so that part of the answer is missing. The Vampire Spawn stat block is also cut off, so its weaknesses aren't covered.

## o31 (Monster) What is the challenge rating of a Lich?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

A Lich has a **Challenge Rating of 21**, which is worth **33,000 XP**. This applies to the standard Lich in the 2014 Monster Manual and, as far as I know, the 2024 rules. I'm not certain whether the 2024 SRD 5.2 includes the Lich stat block, so check the rulebook if you need the exact 2024 entry.

[Rules Glossary > Challenge Rating]
Challenge Rating (CR) summarizes the threat a monster poses to a group of four player characters. Compare a monster's CR to the characters' level. If the CR is higher, the monster is likely a danger. If the CR is lower, the monster likely poses little threat. But circumstances and the number of player characters can significantly alter how threatening a monster is in actual play. "Gameplay Toolbox" ("Combat Encounters") provides guidance to the GM on using CR while planning potential combat

[Rules Glossary > Stat Block]
_CR._ Challenge Rating summarizes the threat a monster poses and is detailed in "Monsters." The Experience Points characters receive for defeating a monster and its Proficiency Bonus follow. [Rules Glossary > Stat Block]
#### Stat Block  
A stat block contains the game statistics of a monster. Each stat block includes the following information presented after the monster's name.  
_Size._ A monster is Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, or Gargantuan. _See also_ "Size."  
_Creature Type._ This entry notes the family of beings a monster belongs to, along with any descriptive tags. _See also_ "Creature Type."

---

[Rules Glossary > Stat Block]
_Damage Notation._ A stat block usually provides both a static number and a die expression for each instance of damage. For example, an attack might deal 4 (1d4 + 2) damage on a hit. The GM determines whether you use the static number or the die expression in parentheses; you don't use both.

---

[Monsters > Stat Block Overview]
# Monsters  
## Stat Block Overview  
A monster has a stat block that contains the rules necessary to use it in the game. Stat blocks are divided into the following parts:  
**Name and General Details.** The name of the monster is followed by its size, creature type (along with any descriptive tags), and alignment.  
**Combat Highlights.** Armor Class, Hit Points, Speed, and Initiative are provided here.
```
</details>


---

## o32 (Monster) Which monsters have resistance to fire damage?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

From memory, these monsters resist fire damage, though I can't check the SRD 5.2 text, so please verify the exact entries:

- **Vrock**: resistance to cold, fire, and lightning
- **Hezrou**: resistance to cold, fire, and lightning
- **Glabrezu**: resistance to cold, fire, and lightning
- **Dretch**: resistance to cold, fire, and lightning
- **Quasit**: resistance to cold, fire, and lightning (less certain)

Many fire-associated monsters, such as **red dragons**, **hell hounds**, **fire elementals**, **azers**, **efreets**, **magmins**, and **fire giants**, are *immune* to fire damage rather than resistant. Immunity is the stronger effect, so check whether the monster you're looking for has immunity or resistance.


### v1_baseline  (3 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

The Context doesn't name any monster that has Resistance to Fire damage.

- **Nightmare:** Its Confer Fire Resistance trait lets it grant Resistance to Fire damage to a rider on it. The Context doesn't say whether the nightmare itself has that Resistance.
- **Anything underwater:** The Fire Resistance rule says anything underwater has Resistance to Fire damage. This applies to any creature underwater, but the Context doesn't name specific monsters.

[Playing the Game > Order of Application]
For example, a creature has Resistance to all damage and Vulnerability to Fire damage, and it's within a magical aura that reduces all damage by 5. If it takes 28 Fire damage, the damage is first reduced by 5 (to 23), then halved for the creature's Resistance (and rounded down to 11), then doubled for its Vulnerability (to 22).

---

[Playing the Game > Fire Resistance]
#### Fire Resistance  
Anything underwater has Resistance to Fire damage (explained in "Damage and Healing").

---

[Spells > Fire Shield]
The flames provide you with a warm shield or a chill shield, as you choose. The warm shield grants you Resistance to Cold damage, and the chill shield grants you Resistance to Fire damage.  
In addition, whenever a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack roll, the shield erupts with flame. The attacker takes 2d8 Fire damage from a warm shield or 2d8 Cold damage from a chill shield.

---

[Rules Glossary > Resistance]
#### Resistance  
If you have Resistance to a damage type, damage of that type is halved against you (round down). Resistance is applied only once to an instance of damage. _See also_ "Playing the Game" ("Damage and Healing").

---

[Playing the Game > Resistance and Vulnerability]
### Resistance and Vulnerability  
Some creatures and objects have Resistance or Vulnerability to certain damage types. If you have Resistance to a damage type, damage of that type is halved against you (round down). If you have Vulnerability to a damage type, damage of that type is doubled against you. For example, if you have Resistance to Cold damage, such damage is halved against you, and if you have Vulnerability to Fire damage, such damage is doubled against you.

---

[Classes > Level 1: Rage]
While active, your Rage follows the rules below.  
_Damage Resistance._ You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.  
_Rage Damage._ When you make an attack using Strength—with either a weapon or an Unarmed Strike—and deal damage to the target, you gain a bonus to the damage that increases as you gain levels as a Barbarian, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the Barbarian Features table.

## o33 (Monster) What special abilities does a Mind Flayer possess?

**Answerable from the SRD:** no


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

A Mind Flayer (CR 7 aberration) has these special abilities:

- **Magic Resistance:** Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.
- **Innate Spellcasting (Psionics):** Its spellcasting ability is Intelligence (spell save DC 15). It can cast *detect thoughts* and *levitate* at will, and *dominate monster* and *plane shift* (self only) once per day each, without material components.
- **Mind Blast (Recharge 5–6):** Each creature in a 60-foot cone must make an Intelligence saving throw (DC 15). On a failure, a creature takes psychic damage and is stunned for 1 minute, and it can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns to end the effect.
- **Tentacles:** Its melee attack deals psychic damage. If the target is Medium or smaller, the target is grappled, and on a failed Intelligence save it is stunned until the grapple ends.
- **Extract Brain:** Against a grappled, stunned humanoid, the mind flayer can extract and devour its brain, which kills the target outright or deals massive damage if it survives.
- **Telepathy:** It can communicate telepathically with creatures within 120 feet.

I'm not fully certain of the exact numbers and wording in the 2024 SRD 5.2 stat block, so check the book if precision matters.

## o34 (Monster) What is the difference between a Goblin and a Hobgoblin?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

**Goblin** (CR 1/4) and **Hobgoblin** (CR 1/2) are both goblinoids, but the hobgoblin is the tougher, more disciplined soldier.

| Feature | Goblin | Hobgoblin |
|---|---|---|
| Size | Small | Medium |
| Challenge | 1/4 | 1/2 |
| Hit Points | 7 (2d6) | 11 (2d8 + 2) |
| Armor Class | 15 (leather armor, shield) | 18 (chain mail, shield) |
| Key trait | **Nimble Escape**: can Disengage or Hide as a bonus action | **Martial Advantage**: once per turn, deals extra 2d6 damage when an ally is within 5 feet of the target |
| Main attacks | Scimitar (+4, 1d6 + 2 Slashing); Shortbow (+4, 1d6 + 2 Piercing, range 80/320 ft) | Longsword (+3, 1d8 + 1 Slashing); Longbow (+3, 1d8 + 1 Piercing, range 150/600 ft) |

In short, goblins are small, nimble skirmishers, while hobgoblins are Medium, sturdier fighters who gain extra damage by fighting alongside allies. These are my best recollection of the classic statblocks, so check the current Monster Manual if exact numbers matter for your game.


### v1_baseline  (3 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

The Context doesn't say what the difference is. It only gives partial information about each creature:

- **Goblin:** Has the Redirect Attack reaction. When a creature it can see attacks it, the goblin can swap places with a Small or Medium ally within 5 feet, and that ally becomes the target instead.
- **Hobgoblin:** Has the Aura of Authority trait, which gives the hobgoblin and its allies Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws while within a 10-foot Emanation, as long as the hobgoblin isn't Incapacitated. It also has the Pack Tactics trait, which gives it Advantage on attack rolls against a creature that has an ally of the hobgoblin within 5 feet of it, if that ally isn't Incapacitated.

The Context lacks the goblin's and hobgoblin's other traits, actions, size, stat blocks, and descriptions, so I can't compare them fully.

[Monsters > Stat Block Overview]
# Monsters  
## Stat Block Overview  
A monster has a stat block that contains the rules necessary to use it in the game. Stat blocks are divided into the following parts:  
**Name and General Details.** The name of the monster is followed by its size, creature type (along with any descriptive tags), and alignment.  
**Combat Highlights.** Armor Class, Hit Points, Speed, and Initiative are provided here.

---

[Monsters > Gear]
### Gear  
Monsters have proficiency with their equipment. If a monster has equipment that can be given away or retrieved, the items are listed in the Gear entry. The monster's stat block might include special flourishes that happen when the monster uses an item, and the stat block might ignore the rules in "Equipment" for that item. When used by someone else, a retrievable item uses its "Equipment" rules, ignoring any special flourishes in the stat block.

---

[Rules Glossary > Stat Block]
#### Stat Block  
A stat block contains the game statistics of a monster. Each stat block includes the following information presented after the monster's name.  
_Size._ A monster is Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, or Gargantuan. _See also_ "Size."  
_Creature Type._ This entry notes the family of beings a monster belongs to, along with any descriptive tags. _See also_ "Creature Type."

---

[Character Origins > Gnome]
#### Gnome  
**Creature Type:** Humanoid
**Size:** Small (about 3–4 feet tall)
**Speed:** 30 feet  
As a Gnome, you have these special traits.  
_Darkvision._ You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.  
_Gnomish Cunning._ You have Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

[Playing the Game > Creature Size]
#### Creature Size  
A creature belongs to a size category, which determines the width of the square space the creature occupies on a map, as shown on the Creature Size and Space table. That table lists the sizes from smallest (Tiny) to largest (Gargantuan). A creature's space is the area that it effectively controls in combat and the area it needs to fight effectively.  
A character's size is determined by species, and a monster's size is specified in the monster's stat block.

[Monsters A–Z > Traits]
#### Traits  
<hr>  
**_Pack Tactics._** The hobgoblin has Advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the hobgoblin's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

---

[Monsters A–Z > Traits]
#### Traits  
<hr>  
**_Aura of Authority._** While in a 10-foot Emanation originating from the hobgoblin, the hobgoblin and its allies have Advantage on attack rolls and saving throws, provided the hobgoblin doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

---

[Character Origins > Ability Scores]
#### Ability Scores  
A background lists three of your character's ability scores. Increase one by 2 and another one by 1, or increase all three by 1. None of these increases can raise a score above 20.

---

[Character Creation > Adjust Ability Scores]
#### Adjust Ability Scores  
After assigning your ability scores, adjust them according to your background. Your background lists three abilities; increase one of those scores by 2 and a different one by 1, or increase all three by 1. None of these increases can raise a score above 20.  
Some players like to increase their class's primary ability, while others prefer to increase a low score.

---

[Feats > Boon of the Night Spirit]
#### Boon of the Night Spirit  
_Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+)_  
You gain the following benefits.  
_Ability Score Increase._ Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 30.  
_Merge with Shadows._ While within Dim Light or Darkness, you can give yourself the Invisible condition as a Bonus Action. The condition ends on you immediately after you take an action, a Bonus Action, or a Reaction.

### Alignment  
The alignment specified in a monster's stat block is a default suggestion of how to roleplay the monster, inspired by its traditional role in the game or real-world folklore. Change a monster's alignment to suit your storytelling needs. The Neutral alignment, in particular, is an invitation for you to consider whether an individual leans toward one of the other alignments.  
"Character Creation" describes the nine alignments and unaligned creatures.

[Playing the Game > Damage Rolls]
### Damage Rolls  
Each weapon, spell, and damaging monster ability specifies the damage it deals. You roll the damage dice, add any modifiers, and deal the damage to your target. If there's a penalty to the damage, it's possible to deal 0 damage but not negative damage.

---

[Playing the Game > Damage Rolls]
When attacking with a weapon, you add your ability modifier—the same modifier used for the attack roll—to the damage roll. A spell tells you which dice to roll for damage and whether to add any modifiers. Unless a rule says otherwise, you don't add your ability modifier to a fixed damage amount that doesn't use a roll, such as the damage of a Blowgun. See "Equipment" for weapons' damage dice and "Spells" for spells' damage dice.

## o36 (Equipment) What is the difference between a Greatsword and a Greataxe?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

The **Greatsword** and **Greataxe** are both Martial Melee weapons with the Heavy and Two-Handed properties. They differ in damage, mastery, cost, and weight.

| | **Greatsword** | **Greataxe** |
|---|---|---|
| **Damage** | 2d6 Slashing (avg. 7) | 1d12 Slashing (avg. 6.5) |
| **Mastery** | Graze | Cleave |
| **Cost** | 50 GP | 30 GP |
| **Weight** | 6 lb. | 7 lb. |

- **Graze:** If your attack misses, you still deal damage equal to the ability modifier you used for the attack.
- **Cleave:** Once per turn, if you hit a creature, you can make a melee attack against a second creature within 5 feet of the first and within your reach.

The Greatsword deals slightly more average damage and has the more reliable Graze mastery. The Greataxe is cheaper and suits Cleave tactics against groups.

- **Magic item compatibility:** The Greatsword can be used with the Vorpal Sword, Dancing Sword, Frost Brand, and Sword of Sharpness. The Greataxe is listed only for the Berserker Axe.
- **Missing information:** The Context doesn't state either weapon's cost, weight, or weapon properties (such as Two-Handed or Versatile), so I can't say whether they differ in those areas. The attack bonuses shown in the stat blocks belong to individual monsters, so they don't indicate a difference between the weapons.

### Mastery Properties  
Each weapon has a mastery property, which is usable only by a character who has a feature, such as Weapon Mastery, that unlocks the property for the character. The properties are defined below.  
> **Improvised Weapons**
>
> If you use an object—such as a table leg, frying pan, or bottle—as a makeshift weapon, see "Improvised Weapons" in "Rules Glossary." Also see those rules if you wield a weapon in an unusual way, such as using a Ranged weapon to make a melee attack.

---

[Equipment > Properties]
**Ammunition.**  
You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

---

[Equipment > Properties]
**Two-Handed.** A Two-Handed weapon requires two hands when you attack with it.  
**Versatile.** A Versatile weapon can be used with one or two hands. A damage value in parentheses appears with the property. The weapon deals that damage when used with two hands to make a melee attack.

## o37 (Equipment) Which weapons have the Finesse property?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

In the 2024 rules (SRD 5.2), the weapons with the **Finesse** property are:

- **Dagger** (Simple Melee)
- **Dart** (Simple Ranged)
- **Rapier** (Martial Melee)
- **Scimitar** (Martial Melee)
- **Shortsword** (Martial Melee)
- **Whip** (Martial Melee)

Finesse lets you use your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls, whichever you prefer.


### v1_baseline  (3 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

## o38 (Equipment) What is the Armor Class provided by Plate Armor?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

Plate armor provides an **Armor Class of 18**. It is heavy armor, so you don't add your Dexterity modifier. It requires a Strength score of 15 and imposes disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.


### v1_baseline  (3 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

The Context doesn't state the base Armor Class of Plate Armor. The Equipment > Armor section gives AC only for Leather Armor (11 plus Dexterity modifier) and Chain Mail (16), and the table it refers to is not included.

The Context does say that Dwarven Plate, a very rare magic item that can be Half Plate or Plate Armor, gives a +2 bonus to Armor Class while worn. That bonus is added to the armor's base AC, which is the part the Context doesn't provide.

*retrieved sections:* Character Creation > Note Armor Training | Magic Items > Dwarven Plate | Equipment > Armor

[Character Creation > Note Armor Training]
#### Note Armor Training  
Your class might give you training with certain categories of armor. Note your armor training on your character sheet. Armor training with a kind of armor means you can wear that armor effectively, gaining defensive bonuses from it. The categories of armor are described in "Equipment."

---

[Magic Items > Dwarven Plate]
#### Dwarven Plate  
_Armor (Half Plate Armor or Plate Armor), Very Rare_  
While wearing this armor, you gain a +2 bonus to Armor Class. In addition, if an effect moves you against your will along the ground, you can take a Reaction to reduce the distance you are moved by up to 10 feet.

---

[Equipment > Armor]
**Armor Class (AC).** The table's Armor Class column tells you what your base AC is when you wear a type of armor. For example, if you wear Leather Armor, your base AC is 11 plus your Dexterity modifier, whereas your AC is 16 in Chain Mail.  
**Strength.** If the table shows a Strength score in the Strength column for an armor type, that armor reduces the wearer's speed by 10 feet unless the wearer has a Strength score equal to or higher than the listed score.

[Playing the Game > Armor Class]
#### Armor Class  
A creature's Armor Class represents how well the creature avoids being wounded in combat. The AC of a character is determined at character creation (see "Character Creation"), whereas the AC of a monster appears in its stat block.  
_Calculating AC._ All creatures start with the same base AC calculation:  
**Base AC** = 10 + the creature's Dexterity modifier  
A creature's AC can then be modified by armor, magic items, spells, and more.

## o39 (Equipment) Which magical weapons provide additional damage?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

Magical weapons add extra damage in these main ways:

- **Enhancement bonuses (+1, +2, +3):** Most magic weapons add their bonus to the damage roll as well as the attack roll. Each point adds 1 damage per hit.
- **Flame Tongue:** Activating it (bonus action) adds 2d6 fire damage on hit.
- **Frost Brand:** Adds 1d6 cold damage on hit.
- **Holy Avenger:** Adds 2d10 radiant damage against fiends and undead.
- **Sun Blade:** Adds radiant damage on hit, plus extra damage in some cases. I'm less certain of the exact dice here.
- **Slayer weapons (e.g., Giant Slayer, Dragon Slayer):** Add extra damage against a specific creature type.

Exact dice, activation requirements, and attunement can vary between editions and supplements, so check the specific item's entry in the *Dungeon Master's Guide* or the 2024 SRD before relying on the numbers.


### v1_baseline  (3 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

Based on the Context, three magic weapons provide additional damage:

- **Vicious Weapon** (any simple or martial weapon): deals an extra 2d6 damage of the same type as the weapon's normal damage to any creature it hits.
- **Sword of Wounding** (glaive, greatsword, longsword, rapier, scimitar, or shortsword): deals an extra 2d6 Necrotic damage on a hit.
- **Sword of Sharpness** (glaive, greatsword, longsword, or scimitar): only when you attack a creature and roll a 20 on the d20 attack roll, the target takes an extra 14 Slashing damage. (Against objects, it instead maximizes your weapon damage dice.)

[Magic Items > Flame Tongue]
While holding this magic weapon, you can take a Bonus Action and use a command word to cause flames to engulf the damage-dealing part of the weapon. **Ammunition.**  
You can use a weapon that has the Ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition is part of the attack (you need a free hand to load a one-handed weapon). After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

---

[Equipment > Ammunition (Varies)]
#### Ammunition (Varies)  
Ammunition is required by a weapon that has the Ammunition property. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon. The Ammunition table lists the different types and the amount you get when you buy them. The table also lists the item that is typically used to store each type; storage must be bought separately.

## o41 (Equipment) Which items require attunement?

**Answerable from the SRD:** yes


### v0_closed_book  (0 chunks, 1 LLM call(s))

In the 2024 rules, an item requires attunement when its entry says so. Attunement takes a short rest, and a creature can be attuned to at most three items at once. Some commonly attuned items include:

- **Weapons:** Flame Tongue, Vorpal Sword, Holy Avenger
- **Wondrous items:** Belt of Giant Strength, Boots of Speed, Cloak of Displacement, Instrument of the Bards, Robe of Eyes, Wings of Flying
- **Armor:** Armor of Invulnerability, Bracers of Defense
- **Rings and rods:** Ring of Spell Storing, Rod of Absorption
- **Staves and wands:** Staff of Power, Wand of Fireballs

Some of these entries carry extra restrictions, such as a class or spellcaster requirement, so check the item's full description. I'm working from memory, so if you need exact wording for a specific item, confirm it against the SRD 5.2 text.

[Magic Items > Magic Item Rules]
## Magic Item Rules  
Rules for identifying, attuning to, and using magic items appear in "Equipment." Additional rules are presented below.  
_Attunement Prerequisites_. If a magic item has a class prerequisite, a creature must be a member of that class to attune to the item. If a creature must be a spellcaster to attune to an item, the creature qualifies if it can cast at least one spell using its traits or features, not by using a magic item or the like.

---

[Equipment > Attunement]
### Attunement  
Some magic items require a creature to form a bond—called Attunement—with them before the creature can use an item's magical properties. Without becoming attuned to an item that requires Attunement, you gain only its nonmagical benefits unless its description states otherwise. For example, a magic Shield that requires Attunement provides the benefits of a normal Shield if you aren't attuned to it, but none of its magical properties.

---

[Rules Glossary > Attunement]
#### Attunement  
Some magic items require a creature to form a bond—called Attunement—with them before the creature can use an item's magical properties. A creature can have Attunement with no more than three magic items at a time. _See also_ "Equipment" ("Magic Items").
```

[Equipment > Attunement]
### Attunement  
Some magic items require a creature to form a bond—called Attunement—with them before the creature can use an item's magical properties. Without becoming attuned to an item that requires Attunement, you gain only its nonmagical benefits unless its description states otherwise. For example, a magic Shield that requires Attunement provides the benefits of a normal Shield if you aren't attuned to it, but none of its magical properties.

---

[Rules Glossary > Attunement]
#### Attunement  
Some magic items require a creature to form a bond—called Attunement—with them before the creature can use an item's magical properties. A creature can have Attunement with no more than three magic items at a time. _See also_ "Equipment" ("Magic Items").

---

[Equipment > Ending Attunement]
#### Ending Attunement  
Your Attunement to an item ends if you no longer satisfy the prerequisites for Attunement, if the item has been more than 100 feet away for at least 24 hours, if you die, or if another creature attunes to
the item. You can also voluntarily end Attunement by spending another Short Rest focused on the item unless the item is cursed.

---

[Magic Items > Magic Item Rules]
## Magic Item Rules  
Rules for identifying, attuning to, and using magic items appear in "Equipment." Additional rules are presented below.  
_Attunement Prerequisites_. If a magic item has a class prerequisite, a creature must be a member of that class to attune to the item. If a creature must be a spellcaster to attune to an item, the creature qualifies if it can cast at least one spell using its traits or features, not by using a magic item or the like.

---

[Magic Items > Sentient Magic Items]
## Sentient Magic Items  
Some magic items have sentience and personality. Such an item might be possessed, haunted by the spirit of a previous owner, or self-aware thanks to the magic used to create it. A sentient item might be a cherished ally to its wielder or a continual thorn in the side.  
Most sentient items are weapons, but other kinds of items can manifest sentience. Single-use items such as potions and scrolls are never sentient.

---

[Magic Items > Communication]
### Communication  
A sentient item communicates by sharing its emotions, broadcasting its thoughts telepathically, or speaking aloud. You can choose how it communicates or roll on the Sentient Item's Communication table.

---

[Magic Items > Senses]
### Senses  
A sentient item can perceive its surroundings out to a limited range. You can choose its senses or roll on the Sentient Item's Senses table.

---

[Magic Items > Sphere of Annihilation]
The sphere obliterates all matter it passes through and all matter that passes through it. Artifacts are the exception. Unless an Artifact is susceptible to damage from a _Sphere of Annihilation_, it passes through the sphere unscathed. Anything else that touches the sphere but isn't wholly engulfed and obliterated by it takes 8d10 Force damage.

---

[Magic Items > Dragon Orb]
#### Dragon Orb  
_Wondrous Item, Artifact (Requires Attunement)_  
An orb is an etched crystal globe about 10 inches in diameter. When used, it grows to about 20 inches in diameter, and mist swirls inside it.

---

[Magic Items > Magic Item Resilience]
## Magic Item Resilience  
A magic item is at least as durable as a nonmagical item of its kind. Most magic items, other than Potions and Scrolls, have Resistance to all damage.  
An Artifact can be destroyed only in some special way. Otherwise, it is impervious to damage. Learning how to destroy an Artifact usually requires research or the completion of a quest.

---

[Magic Items > Cursed Items]
## Cursed Items  
A magic item's description specifies whether it bears a curse. Most methods of identifying items, including the _Identify_ spell, fail to reveal such a curse.  
Attunement to a cursed item can't be ended voluntarily unless the curse is broken first, such as with a _Remove Curse_ spell.

---

[Gameplay Toolbox > Cursed Magic Items]
#### Cursed Magic Items  
Cursed magic items are created deliberately or originate as the result of supernatural events. Such items are detailed in "Magic Items."

---

[Magic Items > Berserker Axe]
_Curse._ This weapon is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the weapon, keeping it within reach at all times. You also have Disadvantage on attack rolls with weapons other than this one.

---

[Magic Items > Wand of Wonder]
This wand has 7 charges. While holding it, you can take a Magic action to expend 1 charge while choosing a point within 120 feet of yourself. That location becomes the point of origin of a spell or other magical effect determined by rolling on the Wand of Wonder Effects table. Spells cast from the wand have a save DC of 15. If a spell's maximum range is normally less than 120 feet, it becomes 120 feet when cast from the wand. If an effect has multiple possible subjects, the GM determines
